## Goal

Prove on real traffic that the all-opencode off-peak low chain absorbs local-slot overflow, and that it neither widens paid spend outside the windows nor regresses the free tier.

## Work

1. **Baseline** (pre-change window) via the proxy-usage-analysis skill CLI:
   `python3 .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py --hours 24`
   Record: `rate_limited`, `fallback_after_queue`, `empty_response`, HTTP 429/503 counts, per-model token share, `munitoai-free` share.
2. After one full 24 h window post-change, re-run the same CLI and diff the same metrics.
3. In `proxy.log`, confirm `Fallback triggered ... to=opencode-go*` events for low-priority traffic occur **only** inside the `available_times` windows, and **zero** inside the UTC 01:00–04:00 / 06:00–10:00 gaps.
4. Confirm the three opencode keys each received traffic (i.e. per-key failover actually engages) by counting dispatches per `entry=` — `opencode-go-3` / `opencode-go-2` / `opencode-go` map one-to-one to `OPENCODE_3_API_KEY` / `OPENCODE_2_API_KEY` / `OPENCODE_API_KEY`. The log line carries `entry=`, not `api_key_env=`.
5. Comment the parent item (LP-0MVF17VP70053JXX) with the before/after table and verdict, and mirror the table on this item.

## Observation window

- Config change LP-0MVF1FQJR000NH2I was activated live at **2026-10-19T14:43Z** via `POST /admin/reload-config` (no proxy restart, no llama-server change); the 5-entry low chain has been in effect since.
- Baseline was captured over the 24 h window **2026-10-18 14:37:48 → 2026-10-19 14:37:48** and is recorded in the comments below.
- The post-change measurement needs ≥24 h after activation (i.e. after **2026-10-20T14:43Z**) and must include at least one complete cheap window (01:00–10:00 local = 00:00–09:00 UTC) so low routing is actually exercised.
- Sample-size caveat: the baseline window contained only 13 low-priority sessions, so a single night's post-change sample may be too small to move aggregate rates — report the effect size with that caveat rather than claiming a verified improvement.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: Before/after metrics table recorded on the parent work item (LP-0MVF17VP70053JXX) and mirrored on this item, covering `rate_limited`, `fallback_after_queue`, `empty_response`, HTTP 429/503 counts, per-model token share and `munitoai-free` share.
- AC2: Log evidence of at least one low-priority fallback to an opencode entry inside an off-peak window — or a documented reason none occurred (e.g. local never overflowed in that window).
- AC3: **Zero** low-priority opencode fallbacks inside the UTC gap windows (01:00–04:00, 06:00–10:00) — proving no paid spend leaked outside permissible times.
- AC4: Per-key dispatch counts (`entry=opencode-go-3` / `opencode-go-2` / `opencode-go`) show whether more than one opencode key was used; if only one was used, say whether that reflects no 429s or an unexpected exclusion bug.
- AC5: Explicit cost statement: did paid-tier token share rise outside the overlap hours? Yes = regression, record it.
- AC6: Honest sample-size caveat when the window is too small to move aggregate numbers — state the low-priority dispatch/fallback counts the verdict rests on.

## Evidence commands

```bash
python3 .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py --hours 24 --log-dir /var/log/llama-proxy
grep -h "Fallback triggered" /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log* | grep "to=opencode-go"     # window placement
grep -h -o "entry=opencode-go[a-z0-9-]*" /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log* | sort | uniq -c # per-key dispatch
grep -h "priority_routing" /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log* | tail -n 5                    # low chain width (expect providers=5)
```

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-19 (plan): pre-check returned effort XS / risk Low → full decomposition skipped; six automated review stages run against existing content.
  - AC1 now names the metrics it compares and requires the table mirrored on this item (traces Work 1–2 and 5).
  - Acceptance criteria converted from a numbered list to `- AC1:` … `- AC6:` bullets so `extract_acceptance_criteria()` (shared/tree_coverage.py) and the audit/implement tooling can see them; text unchanged. Heading normalised to `## Acceptance Criteria`.
  - Work 4 corrected: dispatches are counted per `entry=`; the log carries no `api_key_env=` field.
  - Added "Observation window" (activation time, baseline window, ≥24 h plus one complete cheap window).
  - AC6 clarified: the sample size behind the verdict must be stated.
  - Added verified evidence commands (patterns checked against `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log`).
  - No child items created: single-session measurement task, a leaf by design (Extra Small effort, Low risk).

data.description:
## Goal

Raise the local warm-context routing cap from 100,000 to 120,000 estimated tokens so that requests in the 100K–120K band are admitted to local routing instead of being bypassed remote, and make the configuration actually bind (the economic-ceiling ratio currently clamps at ~100K, so raising the absolute value alone is a no-op).

## Background (measured 2026-10-20 08:06 → 2026-10-21 08:06)

From the proxy-usage-analysis report (157 sessions, 7,048 requests, 5,541 routing decisions):

- `routing_skip_local` events: 3,249 — `context_too_large` 2,462 (75.8%), `large_context_bypass` 787 (24.2%).
- `context_too_large` = estimated prompt context > warm cap (100,000). These are 44.4% of all routing decisions.
- Local model busy only 21.4% of the window (idle 78.6%), so this is a **context cap** problem, not a capacity problem.
- Warm cap resolves as `min(physical per-slot clamp, economic ceiling)`:
  - physical = `local_model_ctx_size // slots - 4096` (126,976 at 2 slots; 83,285 at 3 slots)
  - economic = `round(0.3815 × 262144)` = 100,001, capped by the absolute `local_large_context_warm_cache_threshold` (100,000)
  - → effective warm cap = **100,000**; raising the absolute value alone yields 100,008 (verified by calling `_effective_large_context_thresholds` against the live config).

## Change required (both parts, else no-op)

1. `server.local_large_context_warm_cache_threshold`: `100000` → `120000`
2. `server.local_large_context_economic_ceiling_ratio`: `0.3815` → `0.4578` (= 120000/262144, so the economic term stops being the binding constraint)

With both changes the effective warm cap is 120,000 whenever the physical per-slot clamp allows it (2 slots → 126,976 OK; 3 slots → 83,285 still binds, so the change is inert while 3 slots are active — documented, expected).

## Expected effect (forecast from the analysis window)

Requests with estimated context in (100K, 120K]: **436** across 26 sessions, of which **175** have `new_tokens <= cold threshold (38,000)` and therefore become genuinely local-eligible; the remaining 261 are cold-cache (`new_tokens > 38,000`) and flip from `context_too_large` to `large_context_bypass` — still remote under the fast profile, since `economic_bypass_serves_local` is off there.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `server.local_large_context_warm_cache_threshold` is 120000 and `server.local_large_context_economic_ceiling_ratio` is 0.4578 in `proxy/config.yaml`, with comments explaining that both must move together and how the 3-term model resolves.
2. `_effective_large_context_thresholds` returns warm = 120000 at 2 slots and warm = 83285 at 3 slots for the live config (unit test asserting both, so the slot-count interaction is pinned).
3. Unit tests cover the economic-ceiling interaction: a config with `abs=120000`, `ratio=0.4578` yields 120000; the same with the old ratio 0.3815 yields ~100K (regression guard that raising only the absolute value cannot silently no-op again).
4. Documentation updated (`docs/llama-router.md`, `proxy/README.md`, `proxy/docs/routing.md`) to state the 120K warm cap, the ratio and why they move together.
5. Test fixtures referencing the old values (`proxy/tests/fixtures/merged_config_{fast,cheap}.json`, `prededup_raw_{fast,cheap}.json`) updated where they assert live-config values, or confirmed intentionally independent.
6. Full proxy test suite passes.

## Dependency

Blocked by / depends on LP-0MSEGPO77005CYCQ (token-estimate multiplier / native-tokenizer fix) — the cap is expressed in *estimated* tokens, so its calibration is only meaningful once the routing estimate matches Qwen3-native tokenisation. That item is completed (shipped v0.1.10; native `tokenizer: qwen3` is live in config), so this work is unblocked.

data.description:
## Problem

The dev-push integration gate documented in the implement/ship skills relies on the repo's `.githooks/pre-push` running `run_tests.py --scope full` at push time. In the main checkout `/home/rgardler/projects/llm`:

- `git config --get-all core.hooksPath` returns nothing
- `.git/hooks/pre-push` does not exist
- `.githooks/` contains `pre-push` but is not wired

Consequence: a push to `dev` succeeds without the full-suite gate executing. Observed 2026-10-21 during LP-0MVHSET0A008VU95 — the push completed in <1s and `run_tests.py --summary` reports the full-suite cache entry as `missing` at the pushed commit, i.e. no green evidence was recorded by the gate. The change itself was verified by an explicit full-suite run (PASS), so no red tree was pushed; the gate simply did not run.

## Goal

Either wire the hook (e.g. `git config core.hooksPath .githooks`, or install it into `.git/hooks/`) or document explicitly that agents must run `/skill:test` manually before pushing, so the 'full suite first runs at the dev-push gate' contract holds.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Pushing to `dev` from the main checkout triggers the full-suite pre-push gate (verifiable via `run_tests.py --summary` showing a cached green entry at the pushed commit).
2. If the omission is deliberate, the implement/ship docs state the manual full-suite requirement instead, and `run_tests.py --summary` guidance is updated accordingly.

## Context

The cache-miss behaviour is itself a documented signal (audit F3 `query_cached()` auto-executes on a miss), so the audit path degrades safely — but the push-time gate does not exist here.
data.title: Pre-push full-suite gate not wired in this checkout (core.hooksPath unset)
